It was the epicenter of the movement towards unification of  the Arabian Peninsula after a thousand years of fragmentation.

textBlocks.text: 2.2  Local Climate

Riyadh has a hot desert climate with hot summers and mild winters. The  average high temperature in July is 43.6 °C (110.5 °F). And in winter, the  daily minimum temperature averages between 8-9 C°. Weather through  out the year is mainly dry but receives a fair amount of rain in March and  April. The low humidity helps easing the effects of both heat and cold. It is also  known to have dust storms during these two months.

textBlocks.text: The pedestrian bridge will serve as a connection between the P2  South Business Park Carpark and Diriyah Northern  Cultural District (NCD) public realm located adjacent to the MOC HQ. The bridge will span over the upgraded Prince  Sattam Road and will stand as an iconic landmark at the entrance to Diriyah Gate enhancing the visual charm of  the area. The bridge design should reflect the traditional Najdi language of the development and stand as an iconc  najdi bridge. Its primary purpose is to provide a functional and secure passage for MoC staff during the week days,  but also for pedestrians and cyclists by ensuring a smooth and efficient transition. To ensure accessibility for all  users, the bridge will incorporate required vertical transportations such lifts, travelators, and escalators. The  enclosed, climate controlled bridge will be designed to create a visually stunning structure that complements the  local context and adds a distinctive architectural element to the area (traditional Najdi). The design will carefully  consider the surrounding environment, taking into account the architectural style, materials, levels, and color  palette of the adjacent structures. The bridge’s design will not only harmonize with its surroundings but also  enhance the visual appeal of the area.  Incorporating public art installations or artistic features into the bridge design will provide visitors  with a visually  and culturally captivating design. The design elements will be thoughtfully sensitive to the local cultural context  embedded within the Diriyah Gate masterplan. The overall design of the bridge will respect and reflect the cultural  heritage, blending harmoniously with the surrounding environment.

textBlocks.text: 6.7 Landscape Design

The character of the landscape proposal, and its plant species strategy, should respect the district specific  landscape mood and guidelines. •	 The landscape proposal should be designed to create a cohesive visual identity for the entire site and  complement the surrounding context of the district. •	 The design should be sensitive to the site’s historical and cultural significance. •	 The plant selection should be based on the specific microclimates and soil conditions of the site, ensuring their  long-term viability and sustainability. •	 The design should prioritize the use of drought-tolerant and low-maintenance plants to reduce water  consumption and maintenance costs. •	 The design should include strategies for managing stormwater runoff, such as bioswales and rain gardens. •	 The landscape design should consider the needs of all users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles, and  provide safe and accessible paths of travel throughout the site. •	 Lighting should be integrated into the landscape design to ensure safe and attractive night-time use of the site.

1.0  Introduction
1.1  Document Overview
This document is the Design Brief for a Multi-Disciplinary Consultant (MDC) and their supporting design  team for the P2 South Business Park, located in the Events district of Historical Diriyah, part of the  new Diriyah development in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
Above grade assets of the P2 South Business Park will be primarily commercial offices (44,000m2)  with F&B and convenience retail (3,000m2) and its associated services all located above a carpark  structure (designed by others). The carpark has a capacity of approximately 3,400 bays and designed to  serve both Ministry of Culture Head Office and the P2 South Business Park and F&B assets. The offices  will be developed on two and three above grade levels (Up to Ground +3).
The ground floor slab of the carpark has been designed to accommodate Grade level loading along the  eastern side of the floorplate. The remainder of the floorplate has been designed to accommodate a  future Grade + 3 loading.
The MDC team is tasked to provide design services and respond to and challenge the brief and  assumptions made to date. Diriyah Company will provide a carpark constraints pack which will provide  design limits for the MDC. Prior to proceeding into Concept Design, the consultant will submit after the  first two weeks a revised brief based on the consultant findings and early study as the basis for the  Concept Design. All design outcomes should achieve the fundamentals set out within this technical  document in keeping with the design guidelines and other documentation provided.
The Scope of Work is covered under 2 Tasks (which will be covered under separate Task Orders).   Task 1 is for the above grade office, F&B and public realm above the carpark and the integration of the  carpark welcome halls.  Task 2 is for the MoC Pedestrian Bridge connection and its welcome halls.
1.2  Diriyah Company (DC)
Diriyah Development will become the Kingdom’s historic and cultural hub, proudly showcasing to the  world Saudi Arabia’s 300+ years of history through an engaging and inspiring set of heritage,  hospitality, education, retail and dining experiences for residents, tourists and frequent visitors.
Diriyah Development will see 14 km² of the historic town of Diriyah transformed into a global tourism  destination with its main anchors rooted in its historic culture and heritage. It aims to be developed as  an urban, mixed-use development where people can live, work, and visit, inspired by the principles of  both new urbanism and historical Najdi architectural typology. Diriyah Gate Development Authority,  now Diriyah Company, was established in July 2017 to preserve Diriyah’s history, celebrate its  community, and create a hub for Saudi Arabian culture and heritage.
DC is focused on protecting and preserving the Kingdom’s history including the stories of forefathers  as well as the physical heritage, and ensuring Diriyah’s cultural landmarks are complimented by leading  hospitality brands, fine dining experiences and world-class retail offerings.

2.0 Master Plan Vision & Overview
2.1  Context
Diriyah is easily accessible from the airport and strategically located 15  minutes north-west of the Saudi capital, Riyadh. It is ideally placed to  become a historic cultural, lifestyle and tourism hub for the Kingdom.  Diriyah is a town located on the north western side of Riyadh.  Diriyah –  the Jewel of the Kingdom – is home to At-Turaif district, a UNESCO World  Heritage Site. It was the epicenter of the movement towards unification of  the Arabian Peninsula after a thousand years of fragmentation.
Diriyah is recognized as a symbolic center of inspiration for the generations  of leaders that have led the Kingdom since the foundation of the first  Saudi Arabian state. Diriyah Development will become a global landmark  which will showcase stories of authentic Saudi Arabia.
2.2  Local Climate
Riyadh has a hot desert climate with hot summers and mild winters. The  average high temperature in July is 43.6 °C (110.5 °F). And in winter, the  daily minimum temperature averages between 8-9 C°. Weather through  out the year is mainly dry but receives a fair amount of rain in March and  April. The low humidity helps easing the effects of both heat and cold. It is also  known to have dust storms during these two months.

2.3  Illustrative Diriyah Development Master Plan
These assets encompass museums and  cultural attractions built in the traditional  Najdi Style, resonating with the UNESCO  World Heritage Site of At-Turaif. The assets  are spread across Northern Cultural District,  Diriyah Square and Diriyah South, with a  pedestrian corridor spanning an art district  and period village connecting the various  assets.
Retail is envisioned at three different levels:  a district level offering, serving as the central  node of the development, composed of an  interesting network of small scale streets,  Squares, plazas and bazaars; an F&B  promenade, incorporated across the  development in order to ensure street  activation: and community retail which will  serve and meet the every-day needs of  residents and visitors alike.
Educational needs will be catered across a  dedicated university, a number of  professional institutes and schools and  kindergartens that meet the needs of the  local community. The university and  Professional institutions (Academies) are  subject to a separate demand study and  form part of the core assets provided in the  design brief. The provision of Schools and  Kindergartens is being interpreted through  local municipal Standards.
The hotels are resorts are spread across the  site in various locations taking advantage of  key views like Wadi Hanifah or leverage  adjacencies with vibrant uses such as the art  district and Lifestyle District and thereby  complementing the surrounding assets. It is  envisioned that these assets will have a  limited F&B offering at street level along key  pedestrian movement routes.
The live and work offering across Diriyah is  distributed across a diverse range of  typologies and uses. Following the design  brief, these will be designed in the traditional  Najdi Style, interpreted across boutique  offices, government services, town houses,  apartments, villas and branded residences.  All residential clusters will be complimented  with work, civic and recreational uses within  an appropriate walking catchment.
To boost the quality of life for residents and  stimulate a range of activities across the  site, a series of supporting assets will be  curated across the various districts. These  will take the form of a mix of basic  residential services such as retail, schools,  and health services; to more specialises uses  such as high-end sports clubs, mosques, and  educational institutes.

Bujairi: This district will be developed as a  premium dining and lifestyle destination  integrated with cultural and  entertainment offerings. The district will  be surrounded by the panoramic views  of the historic At-Turaif the World  Heritage Site and Wadi Hanifah.
Events District:  This area is designated for commercial  offices, F&B assets and will feature a  public realm space and monument that  will be flexible and adaptable for a  variety of events.
Wadi Hanifah:  Parts of Wadi Hanifah fall within the  overall site boundary. The Final Master  Plan incorporates the high level zoning  strategy from the ongoing landscape  Master Plan for Wadi Hanifah by others.
Diriyah Phase 2:   Previously known as Ajmakan North and  South, Diryah Phase 2 is a new  development of the Diriyah Gate site.

Diriyah South 1&2: Situated south of Diriyah Square, Diriyah  South provides good views to Wadi  Hanifah, hence the urban design  strategy has been to maximize open  spaces, plazas and active roof-scapes  along the escarpment.
Gateway Precincts:  Gateway clusters along the main  interchange have been planned as Mixed  use communities that benefit from good  access and frontage opportunities.
Samhan:  Samhan is envisioned to be Najdi  residential community overlooking Wadi  Hanifah and At-Turaif.

2.5  Master Plan Design Principles
Northern Cultural District: This district will be well situated near  the northern entry point into Diriyah  Development and will enjoy close  proximity with the large and bustling  ‘King Salman Square’ as well as  museums and At-Turaif, the World  Heritage Site.
Diriyah North: This district will be a hub for artistic and  cultural ecosystem. It will be located  between the northern wadi escarpment  edge and the retail district. Meandering  streets, laneways and civic plazas  provide opportunities to explore and  provide the Art District with a sense of  traditional Najdi character.
Diriyah Square: Diriyah Square will be home to leading  international luxury lifestyle brands. A  completely new lifestyle experience for  Saudi Arabia, the retail offering will  combine iconic global brands with  traditional artisan shops and souks, set  within an authentic Najdi village  atmosphere.
Diriyah Gardens: Planned to accommodate the  Museum of Saudi State and the  Arabian Peninsula Museum, MISK  Museum, Islamic gardens,  professional institutions and a  number of recreation facilities.*

Considered  instrumental to leaving a lasting and  sophisticated impression on the guest experience, the  interior journey within  is to demonstrate these qualities: •	 The interior design and planning is to relate to Najdi historical, cultural and social context, and are to and be  inspired by local tradition and culture. •	 The integration between interior and  the exterior is to keep the visual communication open between the two. •	 The interiors are to reflect ultra luxury finishes and spaces.  •	 The Welcoming Lobby experience is a key driver for the guests interior experience, and is to create an incredible  first impression. •	 The design is to primarily maintain and celebrate a reference to Najdi interiors.  However the design team may  re-interpret elements of Najdi traditions and culture, and  the wider Arabian context, in items as finishes,  furniture, art, artefacts, pattern, color, etc., through a  contextual yet fresh approach.
6.7 Landscape Design
The character of the landscape proposal, and its plant species strategy, should respect the district specific  landscape mood and guidelines. •	 The landscape proposal should be designed to create a cohesive visual identity for the entire site and  complement the surrounding context of the district. •	 The design should be sensitive to the site’s historical and cultural significance. •	 The plant selection should be based on the specific microclimates and soil conditions of the site, ensuring their  long-term viability and sustainability. •	 The design should prioritize the use of drought-tolerant and low-maintenance plants to reduce water  consumption and maintenance costs. •	 The design should include strategies for managing stormwater runoff, such as bioswales and rain gardens. •	 The landscape design should consider the needs of all users, including pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles, and  provide safe and accessible paths of travel throughout the site. •	 Lighting should be integrated into the landscape design to ensure safe and attractive night-time use of the site.

•	 Security is to be embedded in the design of P2 from the earliest  stages and is to be coordinated with all relevant design disciplines  to achieve an appropriate balance between architectural design  and security measures.
